target_customer: US homeowners who want to buy a new home before selling their current one, paying mortgage and service fees
problem: Buyers who must sell first make contingent offers that lose to cash offers, so they lack negotiating power.
business_model: Licensed mortgage lender and cash offer program: equity advance on the current home plus mortgage origination and fees

founders.name: Tim Herman
education: Harvard Business School (MBA, left to join YC)

founders.name: Louis Wilson
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in TechCrunch 2021-02-11 and 2021-10-20 and HousingWire 2022-06-23; not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly lending operations, licensing and capital structuring with standard web software; hard parts were warehouse financing and mortgage compliance, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: State mortgage licensing and debt facilities raise the bar a little, but other lenders and cash offer startups could offer similar products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors named in Oct 2021 included Better.com and Accept.inc; CEO said the real competition was the legacy mortgage industry. Rising rates in 2022 cut volume and led to layoffs.

market_need_then: In competitive housing markets sellers favored non-contingent offers; UpEquity targeted buyers who could not make them. Source for the demand claim is the company's own description and TechCrunch 2021 coverage.

branding.domain_note: Uses upequity.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Reassuring and plain; describes itself as veteran-owned and focused on certainty for homeowners.

branding.brand_signature: Veteran-owned positioning around a former Navy fighter pilot founder

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press covered funding and layoffs, but no coverage of the brand itself, community or merch was found.

outcome_analysis: UpEquity raised about $77M including debt through 2021 after YC S19 and scaled to around 90 staff. In June 2022 rising rates and a frozen fundraising market cut refinance volume and it laid off about 10 percent, but it stayed active with licensing and a debt facility into 2025. Outcome is a survivor under macro pressure, with mixed evidence of growth.
notes: TechCrunch says total raised is $77M and total equity $29.15M, which exceeds the equity rounds recorded (7.5M plus 20M), so about $1.65M of earlier equity is unrecorded and no seed source was found. HousingWire calls the Oct 2021 round a $50M Series B; TechCrunch gives $20M equity plus $30M debt (its text has a typo). A June 2025 debt facility and a $200M SVB facility appear in secondary reports, not recorded. Competitors: Better.com and Accept.inc were named only in an Oct 2021 article and a dated 2019 search found no rivals, so the as-of 2019 list is empty.
